change.title: ao-replay/8764-r2
change.description:
fix(mobile): never restore a page over one the user moved to
fix(mobile): hold the update screen during onboarding and pairing
fix(mobile): keep root-level sheets out of the page restored after an update
fix(mobile): compare whole routes when restoring; hide the update screen's hidden half from VoiceOver
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

findings.title: isSetupRoute leaves out /connect, which updateResume treats as a setup screen
findings.body: The PR defers the update screen "during onboarding or pairing". `isSetupRoute` matches only `/onboarding` and `/pair`. The root layout describes pairing as the scanner and then the manual form pushed over it (`packages/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:267-270`), and `TRANSIENT` in `updateResume.ts:40` lists `/connect` beside `/onboarding` and `/pair` as a setup screen. A download that finishes while the user is typing a manual connection will still raise the full-screen update prompt over the form. The update screen and the resume rules disagree about which routes are setup. Either add `connect` to `isSetupRoute` or say in the comment why manual connect is excluded. If `/connect` is reachable from places other than pairing, keep it out, and then the "setup screens" wording in `updateResume.ts:30-32` is the thing to fix.

findings.title: Landing capture and drop behavior is only covered through the pure helper
findings.body: The core of this change is the effect that records `landing` on the first nav-ready render and then calls `restoreAction`. That is a hook with refs and async storage, and no test exercises it. The tests cover `restoreAction(current, landing, saved)` only with hand-fed arguments. Two cases are untested: storage resolving after the user has already navigated (should drop), and `navState.key` becoming ready before expo-router has applied a reopened deep link (landing would be "/" and the stale-deep-link replace would be dropped). A hook-level test with mocked expo-router, the pattern `root-stack.test.tsx` uses for mocking these modules, would pin the behavior.

findings.title: Source-regex test is tied to prop order and exact expressions
findings.body: The assertions match the literal text `accessibilityElementsHidden=...` immediately followed by `importantForAccessibility=...` with exact ternaries. Reordering props or rewriting the expressions fails the test while the behavior is unchanged, and a mistake elsewhere would not be caught. This follows the repo's `*.source.test.ts` convention, so it is acceptable, but a render test that checks the props on the two views would be sturdier.

contracts.action: Restore the saved page as soon as navigation is ready, without waiting for the store config, and drop the restore if the user has left the landing route
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous effect waited for `config !== null` from useApp and compared only path (query stripped) before replace/push. A cold-start notification tap opens pages directly while the machine is still loading.
contracts.before_after: Before: waited for config, then `restoreAction(pathname, saved)` replaced or pushed whatever the user had since opened. After: `landing` is captured on the first nav-ready render, and `restoreAction(current, landing, saved)` returns "drop" if the route changed. Full hrefs are compared, so the same session on a different `hostId` is replaced.
contracts.visible_effect: The user returns to the page they were on after the OTA restart. If they navigate first, nothing is restored. It no longer waits minutes for the machine.
contracts.failure_mode: If `takeResumeRoute()` rejects, `saved` stays undefined and the restore is silently skipped. This is no worse than before. If expo-router applies a reopened deep link after `navState.key` is set, landing is "/" and the later route counts as moved away, so the restore is dropped rather than replaced. This is safe but it loses the restore, and I did not confirm the ordering.
contracts.open_question: Does expo-router/React Navigation expose the reopened deep link in the same render where `useRootNavigationState().key` first becomes defined?

contracts.action: Defer raising the update screen while on /onboarding or /pair, and offer it when the pathname changes
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously the effect depended only on `isUpdatePending` and `updateId`. The foreground prompt path called showUpdateReady unconditionally.
contracts.before_after: Before: the offer fired the moment an update was pending. After: the effect also depends on `pathname` and checks `isSetupRoute`. The foreground "prompt" path checks `pathnameRef.current` too. `lastOffered` is set only when actually offered, so leaving the setup route triggers the offer.
contracts.visible_effect: Update screen does not interrupt onboarding or pairing, and appears right after the user leaves. /connect is not covered.
contracts.failure_mode: No failure. A user who stays on a setup route never sees the offer, and the update applies on next launch. The foreground check path that ends in a download is covered by the effect.

contracts.action: Hide the invisible half of the update screen from VoiceOver with accessibilityElementsHidden
contracts.equivalent_path: The same views already set `importantForAccessibility`, which is Android only.
contracts.before_after: Before: iOS VoiceOver still read the opacity-0 half. After: `accessibilityElementsHidden` mirrors the restarting flag on both halves.
contracts.visible_effect: VoiceOver users no longer hear or activate the hidden buttons or the status text.

summary: The change holds up. I found nothing that blocks the merge and nothing I'd call a defect. I raised three "consider" items. `isSetupRoute` leaves out `/connect`, though `updateResume.ts` treats it as a setup screen, so the update prompt can still appear over the manual connect form. The new landing/drop logic in `UpdateRouteKeeper` has no hook-level test. The a11y test depends on exact source text. One thing I could not confirm: whether expo-router applies a reopened deep link before `useRootNavigationState().key` is set. If it doesn't, the restore is dropped rather than replaced, which is safe but loses the restore. I only read the code, as instructed.
